answer: One wander is one false identity. The lantern is the register of identities, holding one chain of precedent: a row opens only after the applicant has heard every earlier case, one hearing an epoch, each burning one ember. Ember is minted only when a member's work is judged and upheld, so its stock is fixed and slow. The thousandth wander costs a thousand hearings, a thousand wander cost half a million ember against that stock, so the flood stalls when the fuel runs out. No hearing is shared between rows. It breaks if the lantern admits a second chain, or if a hearing can be skipped.
